title: Prefill/Decode Scheduling: fair-share phase split policy and latency-throughput knobs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Latency-sensitive callers (e.g., interactive chat) compete with high-throughput batch workloads. Current prefill/decode single-queue behavior causes large variance: long requests can starve short low-token requests during decode, and prefill spikes cause backpressure that increases p99 latency. Goal: design and implement a scheduling policy that splits request processing into phases (prefill vs decode), enforces fair-share across customers and priority classes, and exposes latency vs throughput knobs for SLA tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook describing policy semantics (phase split, fairness weights, latency targets)
Scheduler implementation behind a feature flag that separates prefill and decode stages on CPU/GPU worker threads
Automated unit and integration tests validating: no starvation of low-token requests, weights respected under synthetic load, falling back to single-queue when disabled
Benchmark showing p50/p95/p99 latency improvements for interactive workloads with <10% throughput regression for bulk streaming workloads (grafana dashboard link)
API surface for SLO hints (client can send priority: interactive|background) documented and backward compatible
notes: Trade-offs discussed in scoping meeting 2026-03-02: splitting phases reduces head-of-line blocking but increases scheduling complexity and KV cache management overhead.
We must ensure kernel-selection heuristics account for changed decode batching patterns (shorter per-batch sequence lengths during fair-share bursts).

Attention-optimization interactions: grouped attention kernels (e.g., flash attention fused path) expect contiguous decode workloads; phase splitting may fragment those benefits unless we co-schedule similar sequence-length decodes.
We will instrument counters for: queued-prefill-count, queued-decode-count, running-prefill, running-decode, tokens-emitted-by-priority, and KV-cache-hit-rate by request class.
planned_work: Design doc: scheduler state machine + fairness algorithm (Draft by 2026-03-05)
Prototype: feature-flagged runtime change to separate prefill and decode queues (2026-03-09)
Perf tests: synthetic mix (10% interactive short-chat, 90% bulk long-gen) in CI harness (2026-03-12)
Iterate on kernel selection: adjust kernel heuristics to prefer small-batch low-latency kernels for interactive decode (2026-03-15)
Rollout: canary on dedicated cluster then staged traffic (2026-03-20 to 2026-03-22)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting. Agreed to use a two-queue phase-split model: prefill queue and decode queue. Decided fairness will be weighted token-credit accounting per customer and per-priority class.
2026-03-04: Prototype scheduler state machine written. Key states: WAIT_PREFILL, RUN_PREFILL, WAIT_DECODE, RUN_DECODE, EVICT. MVP fairness: leaky-bucket credit per tenant.
2026-03-06: Integration notes: JS SDK can add optional 'slo_hint' header. PM requests default mapping to preserve backwards compatibility.
2026-03-07: Engineering review: Helen Cho suggested tracking KV cache residency per request id to avoid premature eviction during phase transitions; added to TODO.

2026-03-08: First perf run on perf-lab shows p99 reduction of interactive workload from 420ms to 180ms under mixed load; bulk throughput decreased 7%. Logged results to https://grafana.redwood/prod/runtime/ENG-7312 (internal).
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): keep default behavior unchanged for existing customers; expose knobs behind rollout flag and runtime config
Design (Jin Park): provide UX copy for Console explaining why some requests might be deprioritized during heavy prefill spikes
SRE (Helen Cho): add alert if queued-decode grows > 10k for > 5m; otherwise risk memory pressure on worker nodes
risks: KV cache churn: splitting phases might increase KV cache evictions and rehydration cost, hurting quality for long-context requests
Scheduler complexity: bugs could create starvation loops if credits are miscomputed
Kernel throughput regression: if we move too many small decodes to low-latency kernels, aggregate GPU utilization may drop and increase cost
mitigations: Add a hybrid mode that coalesces short decodes into micro-batches to preserve vectorized kernel efficiency
Shadow-mode rollout for 2 weeks to collect telemetry before enforcing hard limits
Fallback policy: when KV cache miss rate crosses threshold, temporarily relax prefill/decode separation to allow cache-friendly batching
next_steps: Complete design doc and get sign-off from PM/Design by 2026-03-09
Finish prototype tests and graph p50/p95/p99 for mixed workloads by 2026-03-12
Prepare canary runbook and monitoring dashboards for runtime-2.4 release window
